title: Theme parks: when stories become places
objective: Comprendre une interview radio sur des parcs qui recréent des univers de fiction et comparer des lieux pour recommander une sortie

steps.title: Warm-up: thrill or chill?
steps.student_instruction: Stand on the left if you love roller coasters, on the right if you hate them. Say why in one sentence.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Faire justifier avec because et un adjectif (thrilling, terrifying, boring). Introduire le lexique des parcs.

steps.title: Listening: theme parks
steps.student_instruction: Listen to the radio interview. Note the parks, the countries and one record or number for each.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Audio British Council « Theme parks » (QR code du cahier) ; sans réseau, lire deux fois le script de secours. Prévenir que certaines informations datent : on travaille la compréhension, pas l'actualité des parcs.

steps.title: Language focus: comparatives and superlatives
steps.student_instruction: Complete: Cedar Point has ___ (many) roller coasters ___ my local park. Ocean Kingdom will have the ___ (long) roller coaster in the world.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Comparatif (-er than / more ... than), superlatif (the -est / the most), irréguliers good / better / the best, bad / worse / the worst.

steps.title: Differentiated practice
steps.student_instruction: Complete your A, B or C sheet, then compare with a partner.
steps.facilitator_instruction: A : tableau de comparaison guidé ; B : rédaction d'une recommandation à partir de fiches de parcs ; C : article critique sur le coût écologique et financier des parcs géants.

steps.title: Pair task: plan the class trip
steps.student_instruction: With your park cards, compare two parks and agree on the best one for the class. Present your choice in three sentences.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Fiches inventées avec prix, attractions, distance. Exiger trois comparatifs et un superlatif, et un accord négocié (I see your point, but...).

steps.title: Exit ticket
steps.student_instruction: Write one comparative and one superlative about places you know.
steps.facilitator_instruction: Ramasser ; repérer more bigger et the most good.

sheets.student_content: Complete the table with the comparative and superlative: big, exciting, good, far. Then write two sentences comparing Cedar Point and a park you know.
sheets.facilitator_correction: bigger / the biggest ; more exciting / the most exciting ; better / the best ; further / the furthest. Phrases libres correctes.

sheets.student_content: Read the three park cards (price, rides, distance). Write a 100-word recommendation for a family with two teenagers.
sheets.facilitator_correction: Production guidée ; attendus : trois comparatifs, un superlatif, un conseil final (I would recommend... because...).

sheets.student_content: Write a 150-word article: "Are giant theme parks worth it?" Think about money, the environment and fun.
sheets.facilitator_correction: Production libre ; attendus : deux arguments opposés, connecteurs (whereas, however, on the other hand), conclusion personnelle.

criteria: L'élève relève des noms de parcs, des pays et des chiffres
L'élève compare deux lieux avec des comparatifs corrects

common_errors: the most good (au lieu de the best)
